chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Zurarah, from Salim ibn Abi Hafsa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, Allah the Exalted says: 'There is nothing for which I have not appointed a guarantor to collect it other than Me, except for charity (Sadaqah), for I receive it with My own hand. So much so that a man may give charity with a single date or half a date, and I nurture it, just as a man nurtures his young camel and its offspring, until they meet him on the Day of Resurrection, and it is like the mountain of Uhud and greater than Uhud.'

key_terms.أُحُد: Mount Uhud, a famous mountain near Medina used as a metaphor for great size
key_terms.الصَّدَقَة: Charity/Giving in the way of God
key_terms.فَصِيلَهُ: Offspring of a camel that has been weaned

ai.seo_question: How does Allah multiply the reward of small charitable acts according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith qudsi, recorded in Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, highlights the divine guarantee of charity's multiplication, distinguishing it from other worldly affairs managed by created beings. It underscores the practical efficacy of even minimal giving, such as a single date, which Allah nurtures personally until it rivals Mount Uhud in weight on the Day of Resurrection, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on the spiritual potency of Sadaqah.
